5ef71f80c45a36814a62fedd.title: British couple on honeymoon killed in helicopter crash on Greek island of Sifnos
5ef71f80c45a36814a62fedd.author: Sofia Ferreira Santos
5ef71f80c45a36814a62fedd.content:
Plume of black smoke seen at site of deadly helicopter crash
- Published
A young British couple and their pilot were killed in a helicopter crash on the Greek island of Sifnos on Monday, Greek police have said.
They have been named as newlyweds Alexander Cromie and Marie Ebert, who were in Greece on their honeymoon.
The private helicopter crashed just metres from a landing pad, killing the pair and their pilot, a Greek national.
The couple are said to have taken the helicopter from the village of Markopoulo near Athens to the popular holiday island, Kathimerini reported.
Greece's aviation safety authority told the BBC it was investigating the crash and that its investigators were heading to the scene on Tuesday to gather evidence and speak to witnesses.
![Two-panel map of Greece showing the location of an approximate crash site near the island of Sifnos in the Aegean Sea. The upper panel locates Sifnos among the Cyclades islands southeast of Athens, with Athens and Markopoulo labelled. An inset map of Greece highlights the area shown. The lower panel is a satellite image of Sifnos, with a callout marking the âApproximate location of crashâ on the islandâs eastern coast. Scale bars indicate 20 km and 10 miles on the regional map, and 2 km and 1 mile on the satellite image.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1600/cpsprodpb/ddcc/live/164b52e0-9afb-11f1-aed2-8d6da8d75094.png)
The BBC has contacted the UK Foreign Office, the Greek authorities and the aviation company for comment.
Asset management firm Blackstone, where Cromie worked, said in a statement: "We are shocked by the tragic passing of three people including our colleague Alex Cromie and his wife Marie Ebert, who were celebrating their honeymoon.
"Alex was beloved by everyone who knew and worked with him at Blackstone, and our thoughts and prayers are with his loved ones."
A senior police official told the Times that the crash came just before the helicopter's scheduled landing time of 18:15 local time (16:15 GMT).
![A few people are seen working at a blackened site on a mountain](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/2048/cpsprodpb/2139/live/d5d51200-9acd-11f1-a291-b542ee92de7c.jpg)
Emergency services personnel and locals were pictured working at the crash site to extinguish flames
Sifnos' Deputy Mayor, Manolis Foundoulakis, arrived at the scene shortly after the incident and told local news site Newsit there was almost "nothing left" of the aircraft.
He said locals saw the helicopter crash within metres of their homes and had described a "bizarre engine noise coming from the aircraft" as it was about to land.
He said two of the victims were found in the wreckage, while the third was a short distance away.
Firefighters worked to tackle a blaze which broke out after the crash, and the flames had been extinguished by Monday evening.
5ef71f80c45a36814a62fedd.summary: A newlywed British couple and their Greek pilot were killed when their private helicopter crashed on the Greek island of Sifnos during their honeymoon on Monday. The aircraft went down just metres from a landing pad near the island's eastern coast, sparking a fire that was extinguished by firefighters. Greece's aviation safety authority is investigating the incident to determine the cause of the crash.
key_points: Newlyweds Alexander Cromie and Marie Ebert died in the crash along with their pilot.
The helicopter crashed metres from a landing pad on Sifnos just before its scheduled landing time.
Locals reported hearing a bizarre engine noise from the aircraft prior to the crash.
Greece's aviation safety authority is investigating the incident.

782fea32acd0bff59758a1da.title: Muslim woman threatened on London bus says abuse is daily
782fea32acd0bff59758a1da.author: Alice Bhandhukravi; Jess Warren
782fea32acd0bff59758a1da.content:
![Salsabil in a blue niqab and headscarf, standing in front of a blue wall.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/924/cpsprodpb/91a3/live/3cce26b0-9afe-11f1-a27d-25dca26018ed.png)
Salsabil says she is regularly abused because of her religious clothing
- Published
A Muslim woman who was abused on a bus in west London for wearing a niqab has said that she is subjected to Islamophobic abuse on a daily basis in the capital.
"Spitting, barging, pushing. It happens to me every single day," says 21-year-old Salsabil.
"We kind of convince ourselves that this is something we have to tolerate rather than report."
A spokesperson for the Metropolitan Police said that "no community in London should have to endure intimidation or abuse" and the force was "committed to tackling all forms of hate crime".
Salsabil said she was travelling home from central London on 31 July when she was verbally abused because of her niqab, a veil for her face that leaves the area around the eyes clear and is worn with a headscarf.
She got off the bus and said she boarded the next one, and was again subjected to verbal abuse regarding her niqab. The incident was captured on video.
"He was swearing at me for the way I'm dressed," Salsabil said.
"I went to go sit down and this passenger stopped me, again, very aggressively, telling me that I'm not welcome with this veil on my face, that this is terrorism, this is not religion.
"He said that if I refuse to take off my veil that he will take it off for me."
Salsabil said the man threatened to kill her, and another passenger intervened and became embroiled in a punch-up with the man.
She said he was the only passenger who came to her defence.
The bus driver intervened and the man was asked to get off, which he did, and Salsabil got off at her normal stop in north-west London.
"I genuinely thought that I was going to be seriously injured," she said. "I felt so alone.
"I'm so grateful for the passenger who did step in and defend me."
'I haven't felt safe in the past year'
She added: "This happens to me really often. If I reported every single incident, I think I would probably just live at the police station."
Salsabil explained that she chose not to report the incident to the Metropolitan Police, after she previously reported an Islamophobic hate crime and officers "were quite dismissive about it".
She said: "A lot of women do report incidents like this and they are dismissed, and being dismissed is very demotivating to ever approach the police again.
"I was born and raised in London and I've always felt safe... but I think recently, for the past year, I haven't felt safe, especially going out on public transport," Salsabil added.
"We should never justify abuse based on how someone dresses," she said. "If a woman chooses to wear the hijab or the niqab, or doesn't choose to wear any religious clothing, she should never feel unsafe."
![A woman holds a smartphone while sitting on a park bench](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1920/cpsprodpb/fb42/live/c96d6cd0-9639-11f1-870d-5d08c49babb2.jpg)
The incident on the bus was captured on video and has been seen by the BBC
Siwan Hayward, Transport for London's (TfL) director of security, policing and enforcement, said she was "appalled" by the video of Salsabil being abused on the bus.
"No-one should ever have to fear or experience abuse when using our network," she said.
"We are urgently looking into this incident and encourage anyone who experienced or witnessed this incident to contact the police."
A spokesperson for the Met Police said they were aware of the video and were making efforts to contact the victim, and urged witnesses to report the incident to force.
Both TfL and the Met said they took a zero-tolerance approach to anti-Muslim hatred.
Data collected by the Met Police , externalshowed that reported faith hate crime rose by 25% in London over the past year, and there was a 31% rise in reported Islamophobic offences.
London's victims commissioner, Andrea Simon, said she did not believe Salsabil's experience was a "one-off".
"We have to be very concerned that this is something that's affecting particularly those who might be visibly identifiable by clothing as being Muslim or being of a faith background," she said.
"It's really concerning to hear that someone who was subjected to this kind of behaviour felt that they weren't able to report what had happened to them to the police, because they lacked confidence that anything would be done about it."

Another passenger intervened and defended her before the man was asked to leave the bus by the driver. Salsabil chose not to report the incident to the Metropolitan Police, citing previous dismissive responses from officers. Both Transport for London and the Met Police expressed concern over the videoed incident and urged witnesses to report hate crimes.

979da410801df556282c46b6.title: Apple’s camera-equipped AirPods appear in leaked video
979da410801df556282c46b6.author: Jess Weatherbed
979da410801df556282c46b6.content:
We may have our first glimpse of Apple’s rumored camera-equipped AirPods, thanks to a video that MacRumors found in the macOS Tahoe 26.7 Release Candidate. The short video clip features a man — who is wearing the new AirPods — holding up a book with the cover displayed, so that Visual Intelligence can see the book title.
Apple’s camera-equipped AirPods appear in leaked video
A short clip found in the latest macOS beta demos the AirPods using visual intelligence.
![Apple AirPods with cameras demo video leak](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/08/Apple-AirPods-with-cameras-demo-video-leak.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0%2C0%2C100%2C100&w=2400)
![Apple AirPods with cameras demo video leak](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/08/Apple-AirPods-with-cameras-demo-video-leak.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0%2C0%2C100%2C100&w=2400)
A Siri voice-over plays over the clip, saying “with Visual Intelligence, your world becomes savable. See something you like? Just ask me to save it for later.” Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman has previously reported that the rumored AirPods with cameras are designed to take in “visual information in low resolution” and act as eyes for Apple’s AI features, potentially allowing Siri to give turn-by-turn directions or answer questions about the wearer’s surroundings.
The AirPods shown in the new demo clip look like a slightly thicker version of the AirPods Pro 3. That’s what Gurman had predicted, along with longer stems to accommodate the cameras, and LED lights that indicate when data is being uploaded to the cloud. We only get a look at the AirPods from the back in the video, but no lights can be seen on them from that angle.
Given those Visual Intelligence features, the AirPods are poised to compete with other camera-equipped AI gadgets like Meta’s Ray-Ban smart glasses, though Apple is also reportedly working on its own smart glasses too. While the AirPods’ cameras “aren’t designed” to snap photos or videos, the stealthy form factor may exacerbate the existing privacy concerns surrounding camera-equipped AI products, following Meta’s “pervert glasses” backlash.
For now, details about Apple’s AirPods with cameras are still slim. If demo videos are already making their way into Apple’s OS betas, the new AirPods may launch alongside the improved version of Siri, which is expected to arrive in September together with the next generation of iPhones.

02e28e796cc68175f254b4a8.title: Hayden Panettiere: Ex Wladimir Klitschko says family is in 'profound shock and grief'
02e28e796cc68175f254b4a8.author: Paul Glynn
02e28e796cc68175f254b4a8.content:
![Actress Hayden Panettiere (left) and Wladimir Klitschko attend the World Music Awards 2010 in Monte Carlo, Monaco](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/2560/cpsprodpb/a08e/live/b953e5a0-9ad9-11f1-b2f7-5d1639b20e22.jpg)
Hayden Panettiere and Wladimir Klitschko had a daughter together in 2014
- Published
Hayden Panettiere's ex-partner Wladimir Klitschko has posted an emotional tribute to the "talented" late Heroes and Nashville star, who he said has "left this world too soon".
The former world heavyweight boxing champion, who shares an 11-year-old daughter with Panettiere, said the family is going through "profound shock and grief" following her death at the age of 36.
Panettiere died in Greenville, South Carolina, on Sunday and police said there were not "any signs of foul play or suspicious circumstances".
She had struggled for years with substance abuse and audio from police dispatchers and crews said they were responding to a "cardiac arrest" and detailed their efforts to resuscitate the woman after a possible "overdose".
The Greenville County Coroner's Office said crews treated a woman in "cardiac arrest" and her autopsy showed "no signs of trauma", but that the cause of death has not been confirmed.
'Darker side of industry'
Klitschko posted, external that the announcement of Panettiere's "tragic death saddens me deeply".
"She left this world far too soon. Hayden was, although no longer my partner, an important part of my life and the mother of our daughter, Kaya.
"She built an incredible career through immense talent, while also facing the darker sides of a very demanding industry. Nothing will erase the times we shared or the place she had in our lives."
![Hayden Panettiere, girlfriend of Ukrainian heavyweight boxing world champion Vladimir Klitschko, reacts to Klitschko's victory over his Italian-born challenger Francesco Pianeta at the SAP arena in Mannheim, Germany, 4 May, 2013.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/2560/cpsprodpb/0c6a/live/93b0c270-9ae1-11f1-b2f7-5d1639b20e22.jpg)
The pair, who met in around 2009, announced their engagement in 2013 and had their daughter together the following year. They never married.
"To our daughter Kaya, I will always speak of her mother with respect and make sure she remembers the person she was," he continued.
"I extend my deepest condolences to Hayden's parents, her friends, and her fans, who are also grieving today. Young and talented people like Hayden should not leave this world so soon.
"I ask everyone to please respect our family's feelings and privacy during this incredibly difficult time. For now, this is all I wish to say.
"Thank you to everyone who is supporting my family and expressing their sincere condolences.
"Rest easy, Hayden. May you find eternal peace."
Strong bond
Panettiere met Klitschko, who was 13 years older than her, at a party in Los Angeles when she was 19.
After their daughter was born, the actress was hit hard by postpartum depression and was drinking heavily.
Klitschko helped get her treatment but when their daughter was three, he asked her to sign over custody.
Panettiere reluctantly agreed and wrote in her autobiography, which was published earlier this year: "Not being under the same roof with her every day has been the most gut-wrenching experience of my life, and it's hard to describe the layers of emotion, including sadness, resentment, and anger I felt because of it...
"I grieve that I'm not the mother I thought I'd be, and definitely not the mother I want to be. Trust me, no one should ever have to raise a child on FaceTime."
She remained involved in her daughter's life and added that "despite it all, the bond I have with Kaya is incredibly strong".
'Bursting with brilliance'
Since the news of Panettiere's death broke on Monday, tributes have poured in from her fellow actors, friends and followers.
Connie Britton, her co-star in the musical drama TV show Nashville, posted pictures of them together on-stage on Instagram., external
"This was Hayden. Bursting with brilliance, shining so bright," she wrote in the caption.

d7475ae832f87f46e770cb66.title: Guardiola’s row with Walker at Manchester City revealed in new Amazon documentary
d7475ae832f87f46e770cb66.author: PA Media; Guardian staff reporter
d7475ae832f87f46e770cb66.content:
Pep Guardiola clashed with his captain and almost broke down in tears as he railed at players during his worst run as Manchester City manager.
Guardiola stood down at the end of last season after winning 20 trophies in a 10-year spell at the Etihad Stadium. One of the lowest points of his glittering reign came during a testing run in the autumn of 2024, when City lost nine times and won only once in 13 games. Guardiola outwardly showed signs of strain, notably when he scratched his face after City surrendered a 3-0 lead to draw 3-3 with Feyenoord in the Champions League.
Behind closed doors he was also angry and upset with his players, as shown in a new fly-on-the-wall Amazon Prime documentary, A Beautiful Obsession.
At one point he argued in the dressing room with then captain Kyle Walker, who felt he was being unfairly singled out. “You keep saying my name in every meeting,” complained Walker after a defeat at Liverpool. “Every fucking meeting it’s my name. You’ve somehow brought my name into it.”
Walker, who had been voted captain by his teammates, also claimed Guardiola did not want him to be skipper.
Guardiola responded by saying Walker was taking the issue too personally but also showed signs of emotion as he explained why he had extended his contract despite their poor run.
“If I am a problem you have to tell me,” said Guardiola in a broken voice. “I won’t stay here for the money or just for the fact of staying. I extended my contract because I want to be with you. I want to fight. I don’t want you to feel like I’m leaving or running away.”
![Pep Guardiola speaking to Kyle Walker in a break in play when Manchester City played Spurs in November 2024. The two clashed when Walker was captain.](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/661e1db928a879acc88f18e1cf001a908a4d6c8c/414_137_2666_1819/master/2666.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)
Another extraordinary outburst came in November 2025 after a dismal 2-0 loss to Bayer Leverkusen in the Champions League. Guardiola, whose decision to make 10 changes had backfired, threatened to quit in the dressing room afterwards.
He said: “It’s unacceptable this lack of courage, passion and love and desire to win and do it better. I work for you. I leave my life, my divorce and my family is away, and everything for all of you. And what do you give back? The fucking performance you have done. It’s a disgrace guys. I’m really fucking tired. When I see that I’m exhausted, I’m drained. I want to quit.”
after newsletter promotion
Khaldoon Al Mubarak, the Manchester City chair, recently said Guardiola must have threatened to leave “100 times” during his tenure but he too had his concerns after the Leverkusen game.
In a remarkable release of voice notes between Khaldoon and the chief executive, Ferran Soriano, the chair said he was “so angry” after “probably one of the lowest points we’ve had”. Soriano said the response should not be “too negative or aggressive” but “not too kind or accommodating either”.
The four-part series, which covers the past two seasons, also includes some frank boardroom discussions about transfer policy and the long-serving Kevin De Bruyne’s disappointment after being told his contract would not be renewed.

The four-part series also documents boardroom discussions, transfer policies, and Kevin De Bruyne's disappointment over his non-renewed contract.

1abaaaafa716f1260ae7e8a9.title: James Webb spotted a bizarre object just 660 million years after the Big Bang that looks like an enormous star but shines with roughly 100 billion Suns' worth of energy — because hidden inside its star-like cocoon is an accreting black hole, rather than a core powered by nuclear fusion.
1abaaaafa716f1260ae7e8a9.author: Space Daily; Deep Field
1abaaaafa716f1260ae7e8a9.content:
In a Webb image, MoM-BH*-1 is scarcely more than a red point. Its spectrum, however, looks like no ordinary star or galaxy. The object existed only about 660 million years after the Big Bang and radiates on the order of 100 billion Suns, yet the team studying it argues that nuclear fusion is not the power source.
The proposed engine is an accreting black hole buried inside an extraordinarily dense cocoon of gas. Radiation released as matter spirals toward the black hole heats and filters through that envelope, giving the whole object a star-like atmosphere. Astronomers call the configuration a “black hole star,” but the name describes its appearance and radiative physics, not a star with a conventional fusion-burning core.
A red point that disappeared at shorter wavelengths
MoM-BH*-1 was identified in the PRIMER extragalactic field and selected for spectroscopic follow-up by Webb’s Mirage or Miracle program. The survey deliberately pursued risky targets that might be remarkable early objects or mundane interlopers. This one stood out as the reddest source in an area covering roughly 250 square arcminutes.
Webb’s NIRCam detected it in the F356W and F444W filters, while it appeared to vanish at wavelengths shorter than about two micrometres. The source remained unresolved, so “enormous star” should not be read as a direct measurement of a stellar surface. What Webb actually recorded was a point-like light source with a peculiar sequence of colours.
NIRSpec then supplied the decisive evidence. Several features fixed its redshift at 7.7569, corresponding to a universe about 660 million years old under the standard cosmological model. A 4.5-hour prism spectrum and an independent, higher-resolution spectrum showed that the red colour came from a huge change in brightness across the Balmer limit.
The Balmer break was too strong for ordinary stars
A Balmer break arises from the way hydrogen atoms absorb photons around a wavelength of 364.6 nanometres in the rest frame. Stellar populations rich in A-type stars can produce a conspicuous break, so astronomers often use it to infer the ages of galaxies. MoM-BH*-1’s break strength was measured at 7.7, with uncertainty of plus 2.3 and minus 1.4.
That is the anomaly. Standard dust-free stellar populations were expected to reach only about 3. Even the contrived limit of a population composed entirely of A-type stars remained below 5. Across the observed spectrum, the flux increased by more than a factor of 20 from Webb’s F277W band to F444W.
The object also showed broad, multi-peaked hydrogen-beta emission with a width around 3,036 kilometres per second, plus absorption in hydrogen-beta and hydrogen-gamma. A narrow oxygen doublet anchored the redshift. The combination of broad emission, deep absorption and the extreme break gave the researchers more than an unusual colour; it provided a set of physical constraints that a successful model had to reproduce. The measurements and model appear in the team’s primary study of MoM-BH*-1.
A black hole wrapped in a gaseous photosphere
The researchers tested close to a million radiative-transfer models. Their preferred solution puts an active galactic nucleus inside metal-poor gas with a hydrogen density around 1011 particles per cubic centimetre and a column density near 1025.8 particles per square centimetre. Turbulent motion around 500 kilometres per second helps broaden the absorption.
Crucially, this envelope is almost dust-free in the model. Hydrogen gas itself blocks and reprocesses the short-wavelength radiation, producing the steep Balmer break. That differs from explanations in which ordinary dust reddens a familiar quasar spectrum. The finding is consistent with broader work suggesting that many little red dots are young black holes inside dense ionized cocoons.
The black hole’s accretion flow is the furnace. Gas falling inward loses gravitational energy, heats and emits radiation. The surrounding material absorbs much of that output and radiates it again from a much larger effective surface, rather as a star’s photosphere releases energy produced deeper inside. The model places this gaseous “atmosphere” across roughly 10 to 100 astronomical units. It is star-like in radiative behaviour, not in its central power source.
One hundred billion Suns describes power, not mass
A bolometric luminosity near 1045 ergs per second is of order 1011 solar luminosities, hence the comparison with roughly 100 billion Suns. It does not mean the object contains 100 billion solar masses, is 100 billion times the Sun’s diameter or releases that energy through fusion. The number is an estimate of total power across wavelengths, and it depends on how the observed spectrum is converted into bolometric output.
The black-hole mass is much less certain. Depending on which assumptions are applied to the unfamiliar line-forming environment, estimates fall broadly around one million to ten million solar masses, with some conventional calibrations returning still larger values. The authors warn that standard relations derived from nearby active galaxies may overestimate black-hole masses and underestimate their accretion rates in these sources.
Webb also did not see the black hole directly. An event horizon this distant is far beyond the telescope’s resolving power, and the dense gas is supposed to hide the innermost accretion flow. The evidence is spectral: a central high-energy source plus gas with extreme density and opacity reproduces the light that escaped. That distinction matters because an alternative calculation has shown that a supermassive metal-free star can match several little-red-dot signatures, including the hydrogen-beta width of MoM-BH*-1.
A missing piece in the little red dot puzzle
Little red dots appeared in large numbers once Webb began surveying the first two billion years of cosmic history. They are compact and red in visible rest-frame light, often possess broad hydrogen lines associated with accreting black holes, yet tend to be faint in X-rays. Treating all their light as starlight can imply galaxies that assembled uncomfortably quickly, one part of the wider tension explored as Webb rewrites early galaxy formation.
A gas cocoon can join several of those clues. It reprocesses the central engine’s radiation into a cooler, star-like continuum, absorbs X-rays, suppresses forbidden emission lines at high density and changes the assumptions used to infer black-hole mass from broad lines. A separate, exceptionally deep Webb spectrum of GLIMPSE-17775 has now supplied more than 40 spectral lines supporting the same general picture.
MoM-BH*-1 is especially valuable because almost all its observed light appears to come from the black-hole-star component rather than a bright host. The object lies near a young galaxy at the same redshift, but the two are distinct. By adding a host galaxy’s light to the MoM-BH*-1 spectrum, the team could reproduce the mixed appearance of more familiar little red dots. A lower-redshift source nicknamed “The Cliff” independently showed a similarly extreme break that researchers attributed to absorption in dense gas rather than old stars.
The cocoon is a strong interpretation, not a photograph
The evidence fits a black hole star, but it does not make the internal geometry uniquely proven. The authors explicitly describe their model as simplified. The assumed accretion spectrum, gas shape, turbulence and energy transport can trade off against one another, while the tentative variability was measured with different instruments. Future time monitoring, deeper spectra and longer-wavelength observations can test whether the source varies like an active black hole and whether its cocoon behaves as predicted.
If the interpretation holds, the object may capture a brief stage in which a young black hole feeds faster than ordinary radiation pressure should allow. A sufficiently opaque envelope can trap or redistribute the accretion energy, reducing the outward force that would otherwise expel the fuel. The black hole could then grow rapidly before the cocoon thins, revealing a more conventional active galactic nucleus or quasar.
That would address one of early-universe astronomy’s hardest timing problems. Billion-solar-mass black holes already existed within the first 700 million years, leaving little time to grow from ordinary stellar remnants. MoM-BH*-1 does not yet prove one formation channel. It does show that Webb can isolate the strange, buried phase in which a massive seed may have acquired its extraordinary head start.

The measurements and model appear in the team’s primary study of MoM-BH*-1.
A black hole wrapped in a gaseous photosphere
The researchers tested close to a million radiative-transfer models. Their preferred solution puts an active galactic nucleus inside metal-poor gas with a hydrogen density around 1011 particles per cubic centimetre and a column density near 1025.8 particles per square centimetre. Turbulent motion around 500 kilometres per second helps broaden the absorption.
Crucially, this envelope is almost dust-free in the model. Hydrogen gas itself blocks and reprocesses the short-wavelength radiation, producing the steep Balmer break. That differs from explanations in which ordinary dust reddens a familiar quasar spectrum. The finding is consistent with broader work suggesting that many little red dots are young black holes inside dense ionized cocoons.
The black hole’s accretion flow is the furnace. Gas falling inward loses gravitational energy, heats and emits radiation. The surrounding material absorbs much of that output and radiates it again from a much larger effective surface, rather as a star’s photosphere releases energy produced deeper inside. The model places this gaseous “atmosphere” across roughly 10 to 100 astronomical units. It is star-like in radiative behaviour, not in its central power source.
One hundred billion Suns describes power, not mass
A bolometric luminosity near 1045 ergs per second is of order 1011 solar luminosities, hence the comparison with roughly 100 billion Suns. It does not mean the object contains 100 billion solar masses, is 100 billion times the Sun’s diameter or releases that energy through fusion. The number is an estimate of total power across wavelengths, and it depends on how the observed spectrum is converted into bolometric output.
The black-hole mass is much less certain. Depending on which assumptions are applied to the unfamiliar line-forming environment, estimates fall broadly around one million to ten million solar masses, with some conventional calibrations returning still larger values. The authors warn that standard relations derived from nearby active galaxies may overestimate black-hole masses and underestimate their accretion rates in these sources.
Webb also did not see the black hole directly. An event horizon this distant is far beyond the telescope’s resolving power, and the dense gas is supposed to hide the innermost accretion flow. The evidence is spectral: a central high-energy source plus gas with extreme density and opacity reproduces the light that escaped. That distinction matters because an alternative calculation has shown that a supermassive metal-free star can match several little-red-dot signatures, including the hydrogen-beta width of MoM-BH*-1.
A missing piece in the little red dot puzzle
Little red dots appeared in large numbers once Webb began surveying the first two billion years of cosmic history. They are compact and red in visible rest-frame light, often possess broad hydrogen lines associated with accreting black holes, yet tend to be faint in X-rays. Treating all their light as starlight can imply galaxies that assembled uncomfortably quickly, one part of the wider tension explored as Webb rewrites early galaxy formation.
A gas cocoon can join several of those clues. It reprocesses the central engine’s radiation into a cooler, star-like continuum, absorbs X-rays, suppresses forbidden emission lines at high density and changes the assumptions used to infer black-hole mass from broad lines. A separate, exceptionally deep Webb spectrum of GLIMPSE-17775 has now supplied more than 40 spectral lines supporting the same general picture.
MoM-BH*-1 is especially valuable because almost all its observed light appears to come from the black-hole-star component rather than a bright host. The object lies near a young galaxy at the same redshift, but the two are distinct. By adding a host galaxy’s light to the MoM-BH*-1 spectrum, the team could reproduce the mixed appearance of more familiar little red dots. A lower-redshift source nicknamed “The Cliff” independently showed a similarly extreme break that researchers attributed to absorption in dense gas rather than old stars.
The cocoon is a strong interpretation, not a photograph
The evidence fits a black hole star, but it does not make the internal geometry uniquely proven. The authors explicitly describe their model as simplified. The assumed accretion spectrum, gas shape, turbulence and energy transport can trade off against one another, while the tentative variability was measured with different instruments. Future time monitoring, deeper spectra and longer-wavelength observations can test whether the source varies like an active black hole and whether its cocoon behaves as predicted.
If the interpretation holds, the object may capture a brief stage in which a young black hole feeds faster than ordinary radiation pressure should allow. A sufficiently opaque envelope can trap or redistribute the accretion energy, reducing the outward force that would otherwise expel the fuel. The black hole could then grow rapidly before the cocoon thins, revealing a more conventional active galactic nucleus or quasar.
That would address one of early-universe astronomy’s hardest timing problems. Billion-solar-mass black holes already existed within the first 700 million years, leaving little time to grow from ordinary stellar remnants. MoM-BH*-1 does not yet prove one formation channel. It does show that Webb can isolate the strange, buried phase in which a massive seed may have acquired its extraordinary head start.

66239b93b235a6c13ca6cad1.title: One dead and hundreds ill in UK salmonella outbreak
66239b93b235a6c13ca6cad1.author: Michelle Roberts
66239b93b235a6c13ca6cad1.content:
![A box of eggs](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/2048/cpsprodpb/f3f2/live/595da390-9af5-11f1-930b-57cfba7235f9.jpg)
- Published
A person has died and hundreds have fallen ill with salmonella food posioning in an outbreak that UK experts believe is linked to eating food made with imported eggs.
The UK Health Security Agency has launched an investigation, external into the 207 cases it has seen in the past year, with most recorded in recent weeks.
More than a third of those affected - some babies and others as old as 90 - have needed hospital care, with two developing serious blood poisoning. Most people get better without treatment, however.
While salmonella cases can happen any time, this outbreak involves a specific, identical strain.
Diarrhoea and vomiting
Symptoms include stomach cramps, diarrhoea, vomiting or fever. These usually develop between 12 and 72 hours after becoming infected.
Anyone who is concerned should contact their GP or out of hours service in the first instance, says the UKHSA.
Most cases - 199 of the 207 - have been in England, including 47 in London and 38 in Yorkshire and Humber.
Hannah Charles, lead epidemiologist for gastrointestinal infections at UKHSA, said: "We're working with Food Standards Agency and other public health agencies to investigate a salmonella outbreak that may be linked to eggs imported from outside of the UK."
Salmonella can be found in a number of food sources including raw or under-cooked poultry or meat and eggs.
Preparing and cooking food thoroughly can prevent infection, as well as washing your hands after using the bathroom and before handling food.
Thousands of cases food poisoning happen each year in the UK caused by lots of different strains of salmonella.
It is more unusual to see an outbreak like this linked to one specific stain of the bacterium affecting many people at one time.
The UKHSA says "extensive" epidemiological and food chain investigations are ongoing to identify the source but that egg consumption remains the strongest to date.
Some of the food businesses linked to 24 of the cases use imported eggs.
"At this time there is no identified link to UK-produced eggs or poultry," says the UKHSA.
Any extra precautions or preventative measures will be implemented if needed, it says. The risk to the general public is low.
Jacquelyn McCormick, Head of Incidents at the Food Standards Agency, said eggs which are thoroughly cooked and handled hygienically should not present a food safety risk.
She advised: "Infants, young children, pregnant people and older adults should only eat runny or raw eggs if they have a British Lion mark or are produced under the Laid in Britain egg assurance scheme."
People handling eggs, eggshells or egg packaging should wash their hands thoroughly with soap and water, she added.

Over a third of those affected have required hospital care, though the overall risk to the general public remains low. Authorities are continuing extensive investigations, while advising thorough cooking and proper hygiene.

Investigators believe the outbreak is connected to food made with imported eggs rather than UK-produced eggs.
More than a third of affected individuals, ranging from babies to 90-year-olds, required hospital treatment.
Symptoms include stomach cramps, diarrhoea, vomiting, and fever, typically appearing 12 to 72 hours after infection.
Vulnerable groups are advised to consume runny or raw eggs only if they carry the British Lion mark or are produced under the Laid in Britain scheme.

0fd61dcb10adaa8ceb325815.title: Kildare: Officers told not to pursue car on motorway
0fd61dcb10adaa8ceb325815.author: Chloe Gibson
0fd61dcb10adaa8ceb325815.content:
Officers told not to pursue car on wrong side of motorway, says police body
![PA Media A shot of a car crash site showing a section of closed motorway with many emergency service vehicles on the road and debris from the crash.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/news/480/cpsprodpb/a34b/live/3d8de100-99fd-11f1-a7ab-8b30adf0800a.jpg.webp) PA Media
Gardaí (Irish police) were instructed to disengage from pursuing a car as it drove in the wrong direction on a motorway before a fatal crash, the Garda Representative Association has said.
Five teenagers were killed in the head-on crash on the M9 in County Kildare on Sunday morning.
Two women are in a critical condition, while another woman and a seven-year-old boy are in a serious condition.
Assistant General Secretary of the Garda Representative Association (GRA), Tara McManus, told the BBC that garda roads policing officers "do not have pursuit training".
She said officers involved in the Kildare incident were given a command to "disengage" with the car after it took "evasive action".
The crash happened on the M9 Northbound at Junction 3 at about 03:00 local time.
The five teenagers who died have been named locally as Joe Carthy from Athy, County Kildare, Alex McCarthy from Carlow, Kamil Pustkowski from Limerick, Jeremy O'Brien and Jack Kennedy, according to Irish broadcaster RTÉ News.
The injured family - two women aged in their 30s and one in her 20s, and the young boy - are understood to be from Carlow.
McManus said the teenagers had been in the car for a number of hours before the collision and gardaí had attempted to interact with them and bring the vehicle to a stop on "several occasions".
"At that stage our members would not continue in that pursuit and the directions that were given by our command and control centre were to disengage," she said.
"That would be the normal procedure for us that we do not engage with a car that has decided to take that sort of evasive action."
![Social Media A composite image of five young men. Some of them have taken selfies other are pictures that have been taken of them.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/news/480/cpsprodpb/c601/live/eddea4b0-9adc-11f1-a291-b542ee92de7c.jpg.webp) Social Media
"Our roads policing officers, whose speciality is obviously roads policing, do not have pursuit training," she said.
She added that officers could face serious personal consequences if they took action without the appropriate training.
The GRA, which supports rank and file police officers, would support tougher legislation, including harsher sentences and driving bans for people caught engaging in dangerous behaviour on the roads, she said.
McManus also described the aftermath of the crash as "horrific" for the officers who attended the scene.
McManus said gardaí who attended the scene could require counselling for "months or years" to deal with the psychological impact of what they witnessed.
![A satellite image of the east cost of Ireland. Outline on the image is the M9 road, as well as Junction 3 and Junction 4.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/news/480/cpsprodpb/72fc/live/124ff650-9a1f-11f1-aed2-8d6da8d75094.jpg.webp)
Pursuit training a 'critical shortfall'
Brendan O'Connor, a Donegal garda and a former president of the GRA, said he believed the public would be "shocked" at the lack of pursuit training.
"The GRA have raised this for many, many years," he told the BBC's Nolan Show, adding that it was a "pressing police issue" and the "terrible events in Kildare" expose a "critical shortfall" in capacity.
"There has been massive investment in An Garda Síochána, contrary to what's happening in Northern Ireland in relation to [police] funding, but police driver training has just seemed to be on the back foot and not prioritised," he claimed.
An Garda Síochána has been contacted for comment.
Road deaths in Ireland
Leo Lieghio, vice president of the Irish Road Victims Association, has called for greater urgency in tackling road deaths.
Lieghio's 16-year-old daughter, Marsia, was knocked down by a driver travelling at 50mph at a pedestrian crossing in Dublin in 2005. She died in hospital six days later.
He said the families of those killed and injured will be experiencing "torment".
"Their lives have been turned upside down through no fault of their own. They will be going through hell."
Lieghio added that there needs to be a stronger focus on consequences and early intervention, particularly for dangerous or criminal behaviour on the roads.
"We should be looking at structured intervention, something that teaches responsibility," he said.
Lieghio called for a "reform programme" aimed at young people involved in criminal activity on the roads, alongside greater responsibility from drivers and the wider public.
"We all have a responsibility on our roads, and if we see something wrong happening, we should be reporting it. We need consequences for a change of behaviour," he said.
Lieghio said each death has consequences that extend far beyond the person who loses their life.
"I can imagine what's going on in those hospitals now. I sat beside my daughter's bed for six days, praying and hoping for something to change, but she couldn't fight anymore," he said.
'Sadness, anger, compassion and grief'
The parish priest of Athy said his "heart, thoughts and prayers" are with all of those impacted by the "tragic situation".
Fr Seamus McEntee said he travelled along the same stretch of the motorway just hours before the crash took place.
He said the people he has spoken to feel "a mixture of emotions" and are "carrying sadness, anger, compassion and grief".
0fd61dcb10adaa8ceb325815.summary: Irish police were instructed to disengage from pursuing a car driving in the wrong direction on the M9 motorway in County Kildare before a fatal head-on crash. The collision resulted in the deaths of five teenagers and left several others, including a seven-year-old boy and three women, with serious or critical injuries. The Garda Representative Association stated that roads policing officers lack pursuit training and followed standard procedure by disengaging after the vehicle took evasive action.
key_points: Five teenagers were killed and four other people were seriously or critically injured in a head-on crash on the M9 in County Kildare.
Gardaí were ordered to disengage from pursuing the vehicle after it drove in the wrong direction and took evasive action.
The Garda Representative Association stated that roads policing officers do not have pursuit training.
The GRA and other safety advocates have highlighted a lack of driver training and called for stronger consequences and intervention for dangerous road behavior.

709f744554d74d55d7129ae2.title: Rain finally falls in London! Capital rejoices as showers hit city with more to come
709f744554d74d55d7129ae2.author: Matt Watts; Tom Place
709f744554d74d55d7129ae2.content:
![Add Evening Standard as a preferred source](https://www.standard.co.uk/img/google_preferred_source_badge_dark.png?quality=75&auto=webp&width=960)
![UK: DRONE - London parks dry out amid prolonged heat and lack of rain.](https://cdn.ex.co/transformations-account/production/761715bb-261d-4032-af09-a493a82bd926/e635ba55-b89a-5b3d-ac13-c3a16b31b9f4/thumbnail-360.webp)
![WEST END FINAL](https://www.standard.co.uk/img/newsletters/newsletter_we_final_embed_desktop.png)
Londoners woke on Tuesday to puddles on the streets, while others celebrated as they heard the rain in the early hours.
The tracker showed rain hitting most of the city - some parts of which haven’t seen any real rain for almost two months.
![Puddles could be seen on streets and pavements in the capital on Tuesday morning](https://static.standard.co.uk/2026/08/18/5/20/rain-London.jpeg?quality=75&auto=webp&width=960)
It comes after England saw the driest July on record - with no meaningful rain in London.
Across the Thames catchment area, just 0.8mm of rain was recorded - a mere 2% of the long-term average.
Many Londoners took to social media to celebrate after the rain fell overnight.
Multiple forecasters are also predicting more rain to fall in the capital in the coming days, with further showers expected later on Tuesday.
Light rain showers are also forecast for Wednesday, Thursday and Friday by BBC weather, and the Met Office is also predicting a chance of showers on those days.
Read More
Most of the showers will fall across parts of north-west England, Northern Ireland and southern Scotland, with some parts of south-east England staying dry.
709f744554d74d55d7129ae2.summary: Rain finally fell in London on Tuesday morning after nearly two months without real rain, following England's driest July on record. Residents celebrated the showers on social media as puddles formed across the city streets. Forecasters predict further rain and light showers for the capital in the coming days.
key_points: London received its first significant rain in nearly two months on Tuesday morning.
England experienced its driest July on record, with London seeing no meaningful rainfall.
Residents celebrated the arrival of the rain on social media.
Forecasters including the Met Office and BBC Weather predict more showers for the capital through the rest of the week.

d1cafe77c9d026ea0853a059.title: UK pay growth slows as job vacancies hit five-year low
d1cafe77c9d026ea0853a059.author: Richard Partington
d1cafe77c9d026ea0853a059.content:
Wage growth in the UK slowed in June and vacancies hit a five-year low as workers came under pressure from a renewed cost of living squeeze amid the economic impact from the Iran war.
Figures from the Office for National Statistics show average growth in total earnings, including bonuses, fell to 4.1% in the three months to June, down from 4.4% in the three months to May.
The pay slowdown could deter the Bank of England from raising interest rates this year, some economists suggested.
Liz McKeown, the ONS director of economic statistics, said the data showed “some softening” in the jobs market despite a broadly unchanged picture overall, in a potential sign of stabilisation after a sharper slowdown earlier this year.
“Regular wage growth has remained broadly stable in recent months. However, private sector pay growth has continued to ease, while public sector pay growth remains elevated due to the timing of the latest NHS pay awards,” she added.
Pay growth excluding bonuses strengthened slightly from 3.4% to 3.5%. City economists had forecast the rate would remain unchanged. The number of workers on company payrolls fell by 13,000 in July, matching the decline in June after larger falls in previous months.
However, earnings growth, excluding bonuses, in the private sector slowed to 2.8%, the weakest growth rate since October 2020. Pay growth in the public sector strengthened to 6.1%, reflecting the payment of NHS staff pay rises earlier in 2026 compared to 2025, which distorts the figure.
Vacancies fell to a five-year low as small businesses warned they were facing a rise in employment costs. There were 707,000 in May to July, a drop of 6,000 compared with the previous three months and the lowest level since spring 2021.
“Ongoing weakness in private sector hiring and wage growth suggests the bar is still relatively high for a rate hike in 2026, barring a severe and prolonged spike in energy prices,” said James Smith, a developed markets economist at the Dutch bank ING.
Modupe Adegbembo, an economist at the investment bank Jefferies, said there was little in the data to make the Bank of England more worried about labour-market-driven inflation pressure.
“Whilst the adjustment still looks orderly rather than disorderly, we think the BoE will remain cautious around the state of the labour market,” Adegbembo added.
Money market pricing shows City economists expect one increase in UK interest rates by the end of the year, which would lift the Bank rate from 3.75% to 4%.
The headline rate of unemployment remained unchanged at 4.9%. City economists had forecast a drop to 4.8%.
The snapshot comes as households face a fresh hit to living standards as the fallout from the Middle East conflict rattles the world economy. Official figures due on Wednesday are expected to show that a rise in energy bills drove UK inflation close to 3% in July.
Annual growth in earnings after taking account of inflation was 1.3% in the three months to June. However, workers could face a squeeze as rising inflation approaches the slowing rate of earnings growth.
The figures highlight the challenge for Andy Burnham’s government to ease the financial pressure on households before a difficult autumn budget.
The prime minister used his first week in office to announce a series of “breathing space” measures to ease the cost of living, and he has promised to combat unemployment as young people bear the brunt from recent higher rates of joblessness.
Ministers are awaiting a review into youth jobs from Alan Milburn, the former Labour cabinet minister, after the number of 16- to 24-year-olds not in education, employment or training (Neet) surpassed a million earlier this year for the first time in more than a decade.
Before a final report this autumn, Milburn told the Guardian this week that he would call on the government to “turbocharge” the provision of internships for young people with special educational needs.
Earlier this month he told this newspaper he would recommend new requirements for English primary schools to take steps to identify children at risk of leaving education at 16 without finding a job.
Pat McFadden, the work and pensions secretary, said: “It’s encouraging to see signs of progress in the latest figures, with employment on the up and a continued fall in unemployment rate.”
He said the government had put in place measures to overhaul the benefits system and to support people to find work, including a youth jobs grant to encourage businesses to hire young people.
“We will continue to reform welfare and employment support so that more people can live independently and restore opportunity across the country,” he added.
Economists said the figures showed signs of a slowing jobs market that could strengthen the case for the Bank of England to hold back from raising interest rates.
Threadneedle Street has signalled that a weaker backdrop in the labour market could help limit the capacity for stubbornly high inflation becoming entrenched in the economy.
Jake Finney, a senior economist at PwC UK, said: “On the face of it, the latest labour market report looks relatively benign. Unemployment, employment and inactivity remain broadly stable, while vacancies edged down but are essentially levelling off. The jobs market remains soft, but it isn’t collapsing.”
d1cafe77c9d026ea0853a059.summary: UK wage growth slowed and job vacancies dropped to a five-year low in the three months to June, reflecting a softening labor market amid a renewed cost of living squeeze. Economists suggest the data could deter the Bank of England from raising interest rates later this year. Meanwhile, the government faces pressure to ease financial strain on households and tackle youth unemployment ahead of the autumn budget.
key_points: Average total earnings growth including bonuses fell to 4.1% in the three months to June.
Job vacancies dropped to 707,000 between May and July, marking the lowest level in five years.
Private sector wage growth excluding bonuses slowed to 2.8%, its weakest rate since October 2020.
The headline rate of unemployment remained unchanged at 4.9%.
Economists believe the slowing jobs market makes it less likely the Bank of England will raise interest rates.

6e14840a5b9cfd7fe16035d0.title: Apple iPhone 18 Pro Release Date: Discounted Day Re-Enters The September Schedule
6e14840a5b9cfd7fe16035d0.author: David Phelan
6e14840a5b9cfd7fe16035d0.content:
Aug. 17 update: this post, first published on Saturday, Aug. 15, was updated with more details of why the keynote date predicted elsewhere seems unlikely and further parts of the upcoming release schedule.
The Apple iPhone 18 Pro, alongside the 18 Pro Max and the company’s first foldable iPhone, possibly called the iPhone Ultra, are all about to be announced in an event in September, it seems. A new report has now claimed a different date for the keynote which I think is wrong. Here’s when it will really be, along with every other part of the schedule — down to the minute.
Apple iPhone 18 Pro Keynote Date: Sept. 9
This date is the one that is most crucial: once it’s confirmed, every other part of the release schedule slides effortlessly into place.
I’ve been banging on for ages about when I think the keynote will be (read this for details of every part of the release schedule), but a new report from the Australian site Channel News claims to have exclusive information.
“Apple will unveil its first foldable iPhone at its September 8 US launch event but will not release the device to market, with a major Chinese component supplier confirming the Company is battling supply, testing and pricing problems that could see Australia miss out for months,” it said.
I believe that date is wrong — and you can read the research I did to back this up here.
Essentially, Apple has never held an iPhone keynote on the day after Labor Day, which this year falls on Monday, Sept. 7. So, I think Sept. 8 is very unlikely. The next day, though, Wednesday, Sept. 9, ticks all the boxes, and even Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman, who initially said Sept. 8 was the most likely, has switched his allegiance to Sept. 9.
Take it from me, it’ll be held on Wednesday, Sept. 9, at 10 a.m. Pacific, 1 p.m. Eastern, 6 p.m. U.K. time. It will be held in the Steve Jobs Theater at Apple’s HQ in Cupertino.
As for when the keynote itself will be announced, I believe it will be on Wednesday, Aug. 26 — read more about that here.
Apple iPhone 18 Pro: Pre-Orders Open On Saturday, Sept. 12
The date of the keynote usually means pre-orders open on the following Friday… but not this year, it seems.
I hadn’t realized this, but Apple not only avoids Sept. 11 for keynotes, but also for pre-order dates. Since Sept. 11 falls on a Friday, the company’s traditional day for pre-orders, that activity will begin a day later, on Saturday, Sept. 12. Mark Gurman had more on this.
Apple iPhone 18 Pro: iOS 27 General Release: Monday, Sept. 14
The software which is compatible with many more phones than just the iPhone 18 series, will go live before the new phones go on sale.
This isn’t quite set: Apple has sometimes released the software a day or two earlier or later than expected. But not often. Since 2021, the first version of each new iOS cycle has landed on the Monday after the keynote. In 2020, iOS 14 landed on the Wednesday after the keynote, but more recently, Monday has been the day consistently for five consecutive years. As such, Monday seems odds-on to be the day the software will land.
Remember that iOS 27 is for many more phones than the expected new releases. All iPhones that can run iOS 26 will also support iOS 27. In all, there are 31 iPhones which will handle the next software cycle, every phone from the iPhone 11 through to the iPhone 17, iPhone 17 Pro, iPhone 17 Pro Max, iPhone 17e and iPhone Air. Plus, of course, the next crop of iPhones released this September.
Bear in mind that because a phone supports the new software, it doesn’t mean it will have access to all the features that are coming. Apple Intelligence is only available on the iPhone 15 Pro, iPhone 15 Pro Max and later, for instance. And some of the next advanced features are also restricted, such as the new expressive Siri voices for Siri AI which will not work on the regular iPhone 17 or earlier phones, but are compatible with the iPhone 17 Pro, iPhone 17 Pro Max and iPhone Air as well as, again, the upcoming crop of models.
Look out for it at 8 a.m. Pacific, 11 a.m. Eastern, 4 p.m. U.K. time, though it could be an hour or two later.
Apple iPhone 18 Pro First Reviews Expected: Wednesday, Sept. 16
The first press reviews always appear a couple of days or so before the new iPhones go on sale. Here’s when these are likely to appear this year.
I’ve written about this separately, so won’t dwell on it here, but essentially the Wednesday after the keynote is Apple’s favorite for reviews to first appear. Occasionally, that happens on the Tuesday rather than the Wednesday, but I suspect that won’t be the case this year as the keynote is a day later than usual, so a Tuesday review date would shorten the time the press would have to assemble their thoughts. Note that reviews for the Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4, assuming they are announced, could appear on the same day or one day earlier or later.
Expect reviews to appear from 5 a.m. Pacific, 8 a.m. Eastern and 1 p.m. U.K. time.
Apple iPhone 18 Pro On-Sale Date: Friday, Sept. 18
Assuming other dates are correct, this is almost certainly set in stone. It’s always a Friday that Apple favors, in the week after the keynote. The only question is whether the foldable iPhone will launch at the same time — I believe it will — or be announced alongside the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max but go on sale later.
6e14840a5b9cfd7fe16035d0.summary: Apple is expected to announce the iPhone 18 Pro, 18 Pro Max, and a foldable iPhone at a keynote event on Wednesday, September 9. Pre-orders are projected to begin on Saturday, September 12, while the iOS 27 release and the official on-sale date are anticipated for September 14 and September 18, respectively. The event schedule adjusts slightly to avoid holding keynotes or major pre-order launches on dates associated with Labor Day and September 11.

Pre-orders are expected to start on Saturday, September 12, to avoid the September 11 date.
iOS 27 is projected to see a general release on Monday, September 14.
First press reviews are anticipated to drop on Wednesday, September 16.
The new devices are expected to officially go on sale on Friday, September 18.

d09bd5dfe09596ae101c1480.title: Tupac murder trial: Witness tells Las Vegas court 'all hell broke loose'
d09bd5dfe09596ae101c1480.author: Live Reporting Edited by Brandon Livesay; With Shaimaa Khalil; Regan Morris
d09bd5dfe09596ae101c1480.content:
![](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/128/cpsprodpb//vivo/live/images/2022/10/6/0ec4afc9-c8d1-4651-86ed-1eaf4ad5d5bd.jpg.webp) Shaimaa Khalil
Reporting from court
Watch: What we learned from opening statements in Tupac Shakurâs murder trial
A day in court has been a long time coming in the 30-year-old cold case of Tupac Shakur's murder in Las Vegas.
I was inside the courthouse as opening statements began in the trial of Duane "Keffe D" Davis, charged with murder in Tupac's death.
Davis walked in wearing a blue suit, scanned the public gallery and then sat quietly beside his lawyer as prosecutors laid out their case against him.
They say Davis orchestrated Tupac Shakur's killing as revenge for an attack on his nephew earlier that night.
The prosecutor told the jury what they can expect to hear in this trial: "You will learn from Keffe D himself."
That's because much of the case against Davis comes from his own words in his memoir Compton Street Legend. He describes being inside a white Cadillac at the scene of the shooting and supplying the gun that was passed into the back seat and used to shoot Tupac.
Davis's defence says that account was a fictional embellishment to sell books, calling the decades-long investigation "biased, sloppy and incomplete".
The jury on Monday also heard about the crucial minutes before and after the shooting from those who were there.
A former police officer said he saw the BMW carrying Tupac and record-label boss Suge Knight riddled with bullets.
Another witness recalled hearing the gunfire: "All hell broke loose."
But she did not see the shooter.
And the detective who investigated the case at the time said witnesses had "skedaddled" - leaving police with little more info than a white car and a glimpse of what he described as "a black arm".
As the jury hears from more witnesses in the coming days, they must decide how reliable their testimony is - and whether Davis's own words were indeed fact or fiction.
We are closing our live coverage. You can read a wrap of today's evidence here.
d09bd5dfe09596ae101c1480.summary: Opening statements began in the trial of Duane "Keffe D" Davis, who is charged with orchestrating the 1996 murder of Tupac Shakur as revenge for an earlier attack on his nephew. Prosecutors rely heavily on Davis's own memoir describing his involvement, while the defense argues his account was a fictional fabrication to boost book sales. Witnesses, including a former police officer and a bystander, testified about the shooting and the chaotic aftermath.

Prosecutors argue Davis orchestrated the killing for revenge and supplied the weapon, citing his own memoir.
The defense claims Davis's written account was a fictional embellishment created to sell books and called the police investigation flawed.
Witnesses at the trial described hearing gunfire and seeing the bullet-ridden BMW carrying Tupac and Suge Knight.

820c33af2f9294ab00983655.title: Bizarre 'jellyfish spotted on Mars' in resurfaced Nasa images
820c33af2f9294ab00983655.author: Josh Milton
820c33af2f9294ab00983655.content:
![Side-by-side images show a tripod- shaped object on Mars.](https://metro.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/picture-nasa.png?w=646) 
When we think of Martians, we tend to think of little grey men.
But if a resurfaced image taken by a Nasa rover is anything to go by, the aliens that call Mars home are land-walking ‘jellyfish’. Maybe.
The photo was taken by Curiosity in August 2023, 3,924 Martian days, or Sols, into the extraterrestrial explorer’s time exploring the red planet.
The black-and-white panorama shows the 96-mile-wide Gale Crater, an ancient meteor impact crater, with a black, spindly object on the slopes.
Curiosity, a 1,000kg mobile laboratory sent to analyse Martian soil and rocks, frequently took photographs as it trundled around.
Strangely, the dark object was not there in a photograph taken less than 10 seconds before. It was also the final photo taken that day.
The image caption provides no further information beyond saying the shot was taken by the Right Navigation Camera.
Kari Sivertzen, who has for months been rummaging through images taken by Curiosity, flagged the image on the social media platform X last week.
Users weren’t entirely sure what to make of the object, with Sivertzen insisting it wasn’t Ingenuity, a tiny helicopter that stands on spindly legs.
Ingenuity acted as a scout for the life-seeking probe, Perseverance, which was about 2,300 miles away in the Jezero Crater.
Could it be a UFO?
Jean Ward, a Mars researcher, said the ‘tripod object’ could be a ‘potential UFO’, or Unidentified Flying Object.
‘As always, until we get boots on the ground to see these anomalies up close, I can only speculate as to what these objects might be,’ he said.
Another user added: ‘What on Mars is that?!’
While a third user commented: ‘First image of a jellyfish UFO [on] Mars. Great.’
After all, many, many things have been spotted on Mars that, at first glance, shouldn’t be there. From egg-shaped holes and ‘spiders‘ to rolling hills that resemble the ruins of a city and a ‘crowned face’.
But sceptics said that, like those examples above, this tripod-shaped object could simply be a trick of the light or something our human brains are trying to make sense of too creatively.
![NASA image showing 'doorway' on Mars](https://metro.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/SEI_303745495-92ba.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&w=646) 
![NASA?s Curiosity Mars rover took this selfie at a location nicknamed ?Mary Anning? after a 19th-century English palaeontologist in this image released by the U.S. space agency on Nov 12, 2020. Curiosity snagged three samples of drilled rock at this site on its way out of the Glen Torridon region, which scientists believe preserves an ancient habitable environment. NASA/JPL-Caltech/MSSS/Handout via REUTERS THIS IMAGE HAS BEEN SUPPLIED BY A THIRD PARTY.](https://metro.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/SEI_294017766-0e4b.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&w=646) 
Some questioned whether the object was what space officials call an ‘artefact’. Rather than a lost relic, this term refers to smudge-shaped corrupted pixels and other glitches in cameras when taking a photo.
Nasa has been approached for comment.
Sivertzen said in June that he’s digging through the Martian probe archives so he can share anything that ‘captures his eye’.
‘I believe there is life on other planets, and since NASA has found potential traces of life on Mars, it’s the perfect place to look.’
Curiosity hoped the same. The craft has been roaming Gale Crater since 2012, looking for tiny traces of life etched in centuries-old rocks.

- 
						It's just a photographic glitch.
- 
						It could be something explainable, but mysterious.
- 
						I'm not sure what to believe.

- Trump threatens to 'bomb the s***' out of' another country
On February 10, 1989, people in Wiltshire and Gloucestershire craned their necks up high to see a UFO shaped like the gelatinous creature.
Witnesses, who included police officers, said the object was ‘larger than a helicopter with more lights than a plane’.
Similar dangly objects, now known as Unidentified Aerial Phenomena (UAP), have been seen floating above military bases in Iraq.
But sceptics say such objects could easily be a bedraggled balloon or an aircraft.

While some social media users and a Mars researcher speculated the anomaly could be a UFO or a 'jellyfish' alien, sceptics suggested it may be a trick of the light or a photographic camera glitch known as an artefact. The Curiosity rover, which landed in 2012 to analyze Martian soil and rocks, provided no further information in the image caption.

The black, spindly object appeared in the final photo of the day and was absent in a picture taken less than 10 seconds prior.
Mars researcher Jean Ward suggested the tripod-shaped anomaly could be a potential UFO.
Sceptics believe the object is likely a trick of the light, a creative human interpretation, or a camera glitch artefact.

524c2229c2393d702d62bf53.title: Andy Burnham says he's not embarrassed about hoax message exchange
524c2229c2393d702d62bf53.author: Richard Wheeler
524c2229c2393d702d62bf53.content:
PM Andy Burnham says there was "a minimal exchange of information of zero consequence"
- Published
Andy Burnham says he is not embarrassed that he exchanged messages with a person posing as US President Donald Trump's chief of staff.
The prime minister added all politicians face "these challenges" but insisted he did "everything right" in how he handled the security breach.
News website Politico first reported, external that Burnham communicated with a person claiming to be Susie Wiles. Burnham said there was a "minimal exchange of information of zero consequence".
Liberal Democrat MP James MacCleary has written to Parliament's Intelligence and Security Committee (ISC) to ask them to consider investigating what he called an "egregious security breach".
It is understood the communication between Burnham and the person posing as Wiles was in the form of messages and there was no conversation between the two.
Asked if he was embarrassed about the incident, Burnham told broadcasters: "No, I am not because there was a minimal exchange, nothing of consequence and quickly I realised that this needed to be reported and I did so.
"So I handled it in the right way. All politicians are receiving these pressures and these challenges, but I did everything right."
Pressed on what action is being taken to find out who was behind the incident and to improve systems, Burnham said the "correct action" had been taken both in the UK and the US, without providing further details.
MacCleary, in his letter to ISC chairman Lord Beamish, said the security of the prime minister's communications "ought to be an absolute priority".
He added: "We need to understand how this breach could occur, or else risk it being repeated."
On Monday, Downing Street did not say when the messages were exchanged, or how many there were, nor whether they were over WhatsApp or another system.
A White House official told the BBC on Monday that the latest incident "had nothing to do" with Wiles' phone being hacked.
The BBC previously reported an FBI probe into Wiles' personal phone being hacked in May last year.
Wiles, a key Trump ally, told people at the time that her phone had been hacked after an impersonator - or impersonators - used her contacts file to message other top US officials.
Burnham is not the first high-profile UK political figure to have come into contact with an imposter.
In 2024, the Foreign Office confirmed then-foreign secretary Lord Cameron had been the victim of a hoax call in which someone pretended to be former Ukrainian President Petro Poroshenko.
Former Prime Minister Lord Cameron also exchanged some text messages with the impersonator pretending to be Poroshenko, who was president of Ukraine between 2014 and 2019.
The Foreign Office said it released details of the exchange publicly over fears it could be "manipulated".

39d084d50a096dab94c53104.title: State pension on course to rise by £500 next year
39d084d50a096dab94c53104.author: Rob White
39d084d50a096dab94c53104.content:
Retirees could receive a £500 boost to their state pension next year if wage growth continues to outpace inflation, figures suggest.
The new state pension is on course to rise by £515 to £13,062 and the basic state pension by £395 to £10,010 from next year, according to Hargreaves Lansdown.
The benefit is expected to increase at the same rate as wages for the fourth successive year, boosting pensioners’ payouts by around 4.1pc.
Both payments increase each year by the highest of wage growth, inflation or 2.5pc, thanks to the triple lock.
The annual state pension increase has been tied to wage growth for the past three years, resulting in boosts of up to 8.5pc.

c8c6da0a6dd8bbb6e8193dab.title: Watch European astronaut make history during spacewalk today
c8c6da0a6dd8bbb6e8193dab.author: Mike Wall
c8c6da0a6dd8bbb6e8193dab.content:
![LIVE FROM ISS: First French Woman to Spacewalk tasked with replacing Space-to-Ground Antenna - YouTube](https://img.youtube.com/vi/gXwLYq2ZsLM/maxresdefault.jpg) 
Sophie Adenot will make spaceflight history today (Aug. 18).
The European Space Agency (ESA) astronaut will become the first French woman ever to conduct a spacewalk, an activity she'll undertake with NASA astronaut Anil Menon.
The duo are scheduled to step outside the International Space Station (ISS) for a 6.5-hour excursion today at around 8:35 a.m. EDT (1235 GMT). You can watch it live here at Space.com, courtesy of NASA. Coverage starts at 7 a.m. EDT (1100 GMT).
 ![a smiling woman in a white polo shirt sits in front of black drapes](https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/2zC5KQaMAC25gNRST9USCh.jpg) 
Adenot and Menon will "replace a space-to-ground antenna on the orbital complex," NASA officials wrote in a spacewalk preview.
"The antenna is a critical communications link NASA uses to transmit data, enabling high-speed communications between the Mission Control Center in Houston and the space station," they added.
This will be the second spacewalk for Menon; his first one, conducted with fellow NASA astronaut Jessica Meir, occurred on Aug. 6. During that extravehicular activity (EVA), a carbon dioxide sensor on Menon's spacesuit gave "an unexpected data reading," NASA officials wrote in an Aug. 7 update.
The sensor returned to normal after Menon doffed the suit, but NASA took some extra time to make sure there was no serious issue. As a result, the agency pushed his second spacewalk back a few days — from the originally planned Aug. 13 to today.
Today's spacewalk will be the 282nd overall in the long history of the ISS. Menon, who reached orbit on a Russian Soyuz spacecraft on July 14, will be "crewmember 1" on the EVA. Adenot — a member of SpaceX's Crew-12 mission, which reached the orbiting lab in February — will be "crewmember 2."
Adenot won't be the first French person overall to conduct an EVA. That distinction goes to Jean-Loup Chrétien, who performed a spacewalk outside the then-Soviet Union's Mir space station in 1988.
Other male French astronauts, including Philippe Perrin and Thomas Pesquet, later spacewalked outside the ISS. Pesquet also became the first French person to command an ISS mission, taking the reins in October 2021.

2c2695d5002a972bda7c2cd8.title: Cambridge University vice-chancellor heckled at Jason Arday vigil
2c2695d5002a972bda7c2cd8.author: Mousumi Bakshi; Elliot Deady
2c2695d5002a972bda7c2cd8.content:
Prof Deborah Prentice attended a vigil in Cambridge city centre on Monday
- Published
The vice-chancellor of the University of Cambridge was heckled as she was seen in public for the first time since the death of former professor Jason Arday.
Prof Deborah Prentice attended a vigil organised by the campaign group Stand Up to Racism in Cambridge city centre on Monday evening.
Shouting from a signpost in the city's market square, one attendee called Prentice "shameful" for failing to attend another event organised by Arday's students on Sunday.
Prentice previously said the university was "deeply saddened" by the academic's death.
![Dressed in a black turtle neck and trousers, Jason Arday smiles at the camera in a BBC Radio 4 studio.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1800/cpsprodpb/ea6e/live/9024e850-988b-11f1-83ef-33838a09c7c1.jpg)
Jason Arday was found dead in Battersea, south London, on Friday
Arday, 41, was found dead at an address in Battersea, south London, on Friday afternoon.
He resigned from his role at the university earlier this month after facing allegations of plagiarism. He had denied the claims and, in one case, had been cleared.
Asked about the heckling at the vigil, Cambridge University said: "The vice-chancellor attended the vigil to pay her respects.
"She understands that this is a very difficult time for many people. Our thoughts and deepest condolences are with Jason's family and loved ones, who have lost a father, partner, brother, uncle and son."
Concerns over media scrutiny
Arday's death sparked a debate over whether the media scrutiny was excessive or justified by his prominence.
Anger at the level of media coverage he had been subjected to was felt by many of the people who spoke to the BBC at the rally.
Addressing a crowd, Melanie Benedict, undergraduate president of Cambridge's students' union, said Arday had faced "disproportionate public scrutiny" which "would've been unbearable for anyone".
"The systemic issues that academics of colour have to face year on year have been highlighted by the tragedy of Jason's public treatment and subsequent death," they said.
![A woman - Milli Akehurst - looking at the camera with a neutral expression. She is wearing sunglasses and standing in front of a market, with a group of people behind her.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/2560/cpsprodpb/3ad0/live/2faa4f50-9afd-11f1-a27d-25dca26018ed.jpg)
Milli Akehurst's son studies law at Cambridge
Reflecting on the press coverage, the National Education Union's Cambridgeshire secretary Abby Maddison said: "It doesn't feel right, what has been happening to him."
Milli Akehurst, whose son studies law at Cambridge, said: "It really saddens me the fact that as a black mother who has a son that comes hereâ¦ to see this happening is just heartbreaking.
"I think racism played a big part in [what happened to Arday]. He was cleared [of plagiarism], so why did it continue, and why were there so many articles within the last month or few weeks?"
![A crowd of people standing in a market square looking on as they are addressed by a speaker at a vigil.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/2560/cpsprodpb/b95d/live/6a4c6c00-9afe-11f1-a27d-25dca26018ed.jpg)
Crowds gathered in Cambridge's market square as part of a vigil organised by Stand Up to Racism
Tachya Brobbey said she had been "very moved and very upset" that Arday had been "so trodden into the ground by the media".
"Clearly there was a disproportionate focus on him. We know there are others where there have been allegations that haven't had that amount of attention.
"Equally, I can see parallels with people like Caroline Flack where the media go for someone and destroy them. I think there are lots of layers to this but, yes, racism is a feature of it and it would be naive to think it wasn't."
![A woman - Shareena Howley - looking straight at the camera with a neutral expression. She is wearing a black sleeveless T-shirt and is standing in front of a row of shops and a takeaway food outlet.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/2560/cpsprodpb/8deb/live/a044a520-9afe-11f1-a27d-25dca26018ed.jpg)
Shareena Howley held back tears as she spoke about Jason Arday
Shareena Howley, who had met Arday, said: "He was gentle, he was intelligent, maybe he did make some mistakes but did he really deserve that? Did he really deserve to be hounded to death?"
